candidate.title: snDrop-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned snDrop-Seq card and complete upper poster row: pre-isolated nuclei plus barcoded oligo beads → microfluidic droplets → nuclear lysis and poly(A) RNA capture → droplet breaking and bead pooling → cDNA synthesis/amplification → Sequencing-ready cDNA. The Lake et al. nuclear implementation clarifies the RNA target and finished-library/readout boundary. The full crop was inspected: the separately labelled, clipped lower DroNC-Seq row has its own inputs and arrows, with no shared caption, branch or alternative marker grouping it with the assigned snDrop-Seq row. It is neighbouring poster context, so its states, operations and missing captions are excluded from this extraction. The left Single nuclei → PolyA RNA icons identify the analyte rather than an additional preparative route. Drop-seq is the paper-described parent component, and scTHS-seq elsewhere in the paper is outside the assigned schematic.

states.label: Nuclei suspension
features: Already isolated nuclei containing nuclear RNA are the depicted starting preparation; nuclei isolation is not an upper-row operation.
The separate Single nuclei → PolyA RNA / AA(A)n icon identifies the biological unit and polyadenylated RNA target, rather than a material transfer from extracted RNA into nuclei.

states.label: Sequencing-ready cDNA-derived library
features: The diagram endpoint is labelled Sequencing-ready cDNA. The primary paper clarifies that amplified cDNA is tagmented with Nextera XT and indexed before sequencing (correction c_sn_finished_endpoint); those finishing operations are not separately drawn.

The sequenced carrier is cDNA-derived DNA: read 1 supplies cell-barcode and UMI information, and the RNA-derived paired read supplies transcript/gene sequence, including intronic and exonic contributions.

The readout supports gene-associated UMI counts per nuclear capture barcode, with predominantly 3′ transcript sampling. It represents captured polyadenylated nuclear mRNA and pre-mRNA, with shallow coverage; it does not establish an exhaustive whole-cell or total-RNA inventory or full-length transcript reconstruction.

operations.label: Nuclei lysis
operations.description: Disrupt nuclei within droplets and capture released polyadenylated nuclear RNA on bead oligo(dT), changing RNA from intranuclear material to bead-associated capture material while retaining the droplet compartment.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card and complete upper-row label identify snDrop-Seq (snDrop-seq in the primary paper). Its four local operations act on the already isolated nuclear preparation and follow the depicted route. Lake et al. explicitly name this nuclear implementation and support co-encapsulation, heating intact droplets, breaking/recovering beads, then reverse transcription and cDNA amplification. The separate clipped lower row is not an alternative or grouped target of this card; none of its preparation history is assigned to the upper operations. This resolves the previous overextended method boundary while retaining the supported upper-row architecture.
